clue.text: High crime? Glad about Italy acting to clean up

indicators.note: high can mean drunk or crazed, so the word that follows is in no fit state to keep its order
about can mean round and round, in disorder, so these words are stirred together with the rest

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A crime boss on a high is glad to be cleaning up in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High crime' reads as serious wrongdoing, but High is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A germicidal agent kills germs, which is exactly what a disinfectant does when it works to make something hygienic.

clue.text: Scoff huge rolls, getting energy

indicators.note: something that rolls over turns upside down, which in a down clue flips the word above

parts.note: a straightforward synonym
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone wolfs down huge rolls of bread to get some energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoff looks like the eating sense that goes with rolls; here it is the jeering sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To gibe is to jeer or mock, the same meaning as scoff when used as a verb of derision.

clue.text: A record-holder when running, I stage three runs

indicators.note: running letters are on the move, not standing in their printed places

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run, so three runs is three Rs

explanation.surface: An athlete holding a record describes staging a race over three runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-holder' suggests a champion athlete, which the running and runs keep up.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar is the official who keeps births, deaths and marriages on file, literally a keeper of records.

clue.text: Dressed for summer ahead, after rejecting American play hard to get

parts.note: wearing shorts, the classic warm-weather outfit
a team that is ahead is up

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing out, so the American is turned away from the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Someone in summer shorts turns down an American play.
explanation.walkthrough: Ahead gives UP because a team in the lead is up. 'After' only links: the pieces run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are scarce, with demand outstripping what is available, are difficult to obtain.

clue.text: Stuck in Denmark's capital, I need sunshine at first

parts.note: someone who needs sun would say 'I'm pale'

indicators.note: a capital is the head letter of a word, so only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of Denmark

explanation.surface: A tourist stuck in Copenhagen grumbles about wanting some sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' puts the sun-starved phrase before the D. Copenhagen looks like the capital in question, but capital means only the letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaled means pierced and pinned on a spike, so the victim is held fast, a sense of stuck.

clue.text: When there's news, policeman is present

parts.note: the BBC's evening bulletin is News at Ten, so the news comes at ten
DS is a Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: A police officer turns up whenever there is news to report.
explanation.walkthrough: News at Ten is the long-running British evening television news programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attends a meeting or event is present there, so the verb matches the phrase in sense and tense.

clue.text: Go bananas, having flipped

indicators.note: something flipped is turned over, so the word before it is read backwards

parts.note: bananas and bats are both slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy after flipping their lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go bananas' reads as one idiom, but Go is the definition as a noun, an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a go at something and having a stab at it both mean making an attempt.

clue.text: Hotel cutting rent? One has a point

indicators.note: a thing that cuts into another sits inside it

parts.note: rent as the past tense of rend, ripped
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel cuts its rent, and someone concedes that they have a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent looks like money paid for a room; here it is the old past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike on a plant stem, so it literally has a point.

clue.text: Spurning last of scampi in batter — no good!

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the others

parts.note: Geoffrey Boycott was a famous England cricket batsman

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: the closing letter of scampi
NG is a common abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A diner turns away scampi because the batter is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: Batter suggests the coating on fried fish, but it is a cricketer who bats.
explanation.definitionFit: Boycotting something is refusing to have anything to do with it, which is rejecting it with scorn.

clue.text: Cod coming from across the pond by wet ground

parts.note: a bog is marshy land
the pond is the Atlantic, so what comes from across it is American

explanation.surface: Cod imported from America is landed by a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: Cod looks like the fish; in British slang it is an adjective meaning fake, as in cod Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod as an adjective means sham or mock, the same as something false and counterfeit.

clue.text: One's left this area, with slender horse going around

indicators.note: going around means encircling, so the horse wraps the other pieces

parts.note: a pony is a small horse
A is the standard abbreviation for area
trim as in slim

explanation.surface: Someone has left the area, riding off on a slim horse.
explanation.walkthrough: One's left reads as someone departing; it means what a person leaves behind when they die.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrimony is an inheritance passed down from a father, so it is what a dead parent bequeaths.

clue.text: Robyn's on seedy food, accepting such consumption isn't wise

definitions.note: describes the answer as a kind of unwise spending rather than giving a synonym

parts.note: the setter Robyn speaking of themselves: I am, shortened
pulses are edible seeds such as lentils and beans
to buy an argument is to accept it

explanation.surface: The setter eats shabby food and admits such spending is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the setter above the pulses. Seedy suggests shabby, but here it means made of seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchasing on a sudden whim, without thought, is the classic example of rash consumer spending.

clue.text: Hot cakes left, sweet food

indicators.note: to cake is to coat or encrust, so one piece covers the other

parts.note: hot goods are stolen goods
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Hot cakes have been left out, a sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot cakes looks like the noun phrase, but cakes is a verb meaning coats.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a rich German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas, a kind of sweet baked food.

clue.text: Something staged that's long — The Ring

parts.note: to long for something is to pant for it
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A lengthy stage production of Wagner's Ring cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ring points to Wagner's very long opera cycle; it is only the letter O. A panto is a British Christmas family show.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a comic theatre show put on at Christmas, so it is a piece of theatre performed on a stage.

clue.text: Where to find better game? Look round estate, say

parts.note: three-card monte is a card-sharping game
an estate is a type of car, a station wagon
lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: A shooting party asks where the better game birds are and looks round an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Better is one who bets, not more good; round brings the look round to the far side of the estate car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean resort is famous for its casino, where gamblers place their wagers.

clue.text: Unit of soldiers seizing English horse heartlessly

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the soldiers clasp the next piece

parts.note: OR is Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses its central letter

parts.note: a steed is a horse

explanation.surface: A cavalry unit captures an English horse, cruelly.
explanation.walkthrough: Unit looks like a body of soldiers, which the rest of the surface supports; it is a unit of measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: The oersted is the old CGS measure of magnetic field strength, named after the Danish physicist.

clue.text: What instigators of crime do is really by the book

parts.note: so as in very, really
licit means lawful, following the rules

explanation.surface: A paradox: the masterminds behind crimes are scrupulously law-abiding.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit a crime is to urge or incite someone to commit it, which instigators do by definition.

clue.text: Furious to get taken in by crook and deceived

indicators.note: to be taken in by something is to be held inside it

parts.note: con as short for convict
heated means angry

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at being duped and deceived by a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken in looks like being fooled, matching deceived; it is the instruction to place one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cheated on means a partner has been unfaithful, a betrayal and so a form of being deceived.

clue.text: Determined banking personnel finished

indicators.note: banking can mean enclosing, as banks enclose a river, so one word flanks the other

parts.note: tough as in resolute
HR is Human Resources, the personnel department

explanation.surface: A resolute bank's staff have finished work.
explanation.walkthrough: Banking personnel reads as bank staff, but banking is the instruction to flank.
explanation.definitionFit: When someone is through with a task, they have completed it and are done.

clue.text: Uncovered king given check where there's a castle

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer layer, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Charles is the name of several English kings
CH is the chess notation for check

explanation.surface: A chess game in which an exposed king is put in check near a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: King, check and castle all suggest chess; Harlech is a town in north Wales with a medieval fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlech Castle is a famous medieval Welsh fortress built by Edward I, so the town is a castle site.

clue.text: Queen, perhaps, with new place to get liquor

parts.note: a queen bee is a female, a she-bee
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: The Queen opens a new pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen suggests royalty; perhaps signals an example, the queen of a hive.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed Irish or South African drinking den where alcohol is sold illicitly.

clue.text: Succeeded with art including most blue

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
thou art including becomes, in archaic speech, thou addest

explanation.surface: A successful artist includes the bluest shades in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Art is the old verb form used with thou, so art including is the archaic thou addest.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means sad or depressed, so the most blue person is the unhappiest of all.

clue.text: The best drinks Agnes put away

indicators.note: put away means removed and stored out of sight, so the name is taken out

parts.note: sparkling wines from Champagne
taken as written

explanation.surface: Agnes is praised as the best at knocking back drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Put away suggests drinking down; here it means the name is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A champ, short for champion, is the winner, the top performer.

clue.text: Plague in Rome in the year Antony's back

parts.note: anno is Latin, the language of Rome, for in the year

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the closing letter of Antony

explanation.surface: A plague hits Rome in the year Mark Antony returns.
explanation.definitionFit: To plague someone is to pester and torment them, the same as to irritate them as a verb.

clue.text: Yet again, be unsure of defensive work

parts.note: re- as a prefix meaning again
to doubt is to be uncertain

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure once more about a defensive tactic.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a temporary fortification, an earthwork built for military defence.

clue.text: It's put on after bathing in continental climate

indicators.note: in tells you the answer is sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Something applied after a dip in a warm European climate, like sun cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum powder is dusted on the skin to dry it after a bath or shower.

clue.text: Watery drink picked up somewhere in Surrey

parts.note: runny means thin and liquid

indicators.note: picked up is what a radio does with sound, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: mead is a drink brewed from honey

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a weak drink somewhere in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south-west of London; Runnymede, by the Thames, is where Magna Carta was sealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Runnymede is a meadow and borough in the county of Surrey, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: Land located between delta and sierra?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a country in South Asia
second meaning: a code word in the NATO phonetic alphabet, whose letter comes after D and before S

explanation.walkthrough: Delta and sierra look like geography, a river mouth and a mountain range; they are radio code words, and the question mark admits the second meaning is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is a nation, and the same name is the radio code word for the letter I.

clue.text: Stone axes happening to be found towards the west

parts.note: an event that is on is taking place

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means going right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: x and y are the two axes of a graph

explanation.surface: Stone axes are dug up in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: Stone axes reads as a prehistoric find; Stone is the definition and axes means graph axes.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony, a semi-precious gem.

clue.text: Attractive, e.g. on posing in image?

definitions.text: Attractive, e.g. on posing in image?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: pic is short for picture
hot as in sexy

indicators.note: posing means striking an arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A model looks attractive when posing for a photo.
explanation.walkthrough: Attractive does double duty: it is the definition and also supplies the first piece of the wordplay inside the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A photogenic person looks good in photographs, so they appear attractive on camera.
